notes.title: BioShock: The Collection PC Upgrades
notes.content:
[img=https://downloads.2kgames.com/2kblog/bioshock_collection_hero.jpg]

It’s been nine years since Irrational Games and 2K took you on a terrifying journey to the depths of the underwater city of Rapture with [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b]. Five years since you returned to Rapture in [b][i]BioShock 2[/i][/b]. Three years since you grabbed a skyhook and sailed across the floating city of Columbia in [b][i]BioShock Infinite[/i][/b]. All three titles will be available together, remastered for current-gen, in [b][i][url=https://blog.2k.com/news/bioshock-the-collection-announcement]BioShock: The Collection[/url][/i][/b]. 

PC players have a special opportunity to upgrade some of the [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b] titles to the remastered versions. If you already own [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b], [b][i]BioShock 2[/i][/b], and/or [b][i]Minerva’s Den[/i][/b] on Steam, you will be able to upgrade to the remastered version of the respective title(s) for [b]FREE after release[/b]. 

[b][i]BioShock: The Collection[/i][/b], and the free upgrades, launch globally on September 15, 2016 on Steam at 3pm PT (12am UTC/ 8am AEST September 16).


[b]What gets upgraded on PC?[/b]
[list][*][b][i]BioShock[/i][/b] ➜ [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b] remastered including the unlockable video series, [url=https://youtu.be/KqYtJSSqNnc]Director’s Commentary: [i]Imagining BioShock[/i][/url] 
[*][b][i]BioShock 2[/i][/b] ➜ [b][i]BioShock 2[/i][/b] remastered 
[*][b][i]BioShock 2: Minerva’s Den[/i][/b] ➜ [b][i]BioShock 2: Minerva’s Den[/i][/b] remastered[/list]


[b]I own [i]BioShock[/i] on PC. How do I get the remastered version? [/b]

[b][i]BIOSHOCK[/i] ON STEAM:[/b] If you already own [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b], [b][i]BioShock 2[/i][/b], or [b][i]Minerva’s Den[/i][/b] on Steam, the remastered version for the corresponding title will automatically show up in your Steam library as a separate game. You can expect to see the remastered titles begin rolling out in Steam libraries starting at 3pm PT on September 15, 2016 (find out what time that is in your [url=http://www.thetimezoneconverter.com/?t=3%20pm&tz=Seattle&]timezone[/url]). Once it shows up, you can choose to install the original version or the remastered version. 

[b][i]BIOSHOCK[/i] NOT ON STEAM:[/b] If you have a physical copy of [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b] or [b][i]BioShock 2[/i][/b] on PC, or a [i]Games for Windows Live[/i] digital copy, it may take some additional steps to get the remastered version. 

The original [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b] is 9 years old. NINE. That is ancient in computer years. This also means most physical copies didn’t come with a CD key. To get [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b] remastered on Steam, you must provide your Steam profile information AND proof of purchase of the original PC game to [url=http://support.2k.com/]2K Support[/url]. Find out what else you need to submit a ticket [url=http://support.2k.com/hc/en-us/articles/204338213]here[/url]. 

For [b][i]BioShock 2[/i][/b], find the [i]Games for Windows Live[/i] key that was with your digital or physical copy. Activate this key through Steam.  Information and step-by-step instructions can be found [url=http://support.2k.com/hc/en-us/articles/201338163-BioShock-2-Steamworks-Update-Frequently-Asked-Questions]at this link[/url].

Once you have [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b] or [b][i]BioShock 2[/i][/b] on Steam, you are all set for the upgrade starting at 3pm PT on 9/15/16. Want to know if your PC can handle the new remasters? Below are the minimum and recommended system specs for the remastered versions included in [b][i]BioShock: The Collection[/i][/b]. 


[b]Minimum Specs:[/b]
[list][*]OS: [b]Windows 7 Service Pack 1 64-bit. Platform Update for Windows 7 SP1 and Windows Server 2008 R2 SP1[/b]
[*]Processor: Intel E6750 Core 2 Duo 2.66 GHz / AMD Athlon X2 2.7 GHZ
[*]Memory: 4 GB
[*]Hard Drive: [b][i]BioShock[/i] 25GB; [i]BioShock 2[/i] 25GB; [i]BioShock Infinite[/i] 20GB; Total for all three games 70GB[/b]
[*]Video Card: DirectX11 Compatible, 2GB AMD Radeon HD 7770 / 2GB NVIDIA GeForce GTX 670 
[*]Sound Card: DirectX Compatible Sound Device
[*][b]Other Requirements:[/b] Software installations required including DirectX and Microsoft Visual C++ 2010 & 2012 Redistributable Package. [/list]

[b]Recommended Specs: [/b]
[list][*]OS: [b]Windows 7 Service Pack 1 64-bit. Platform Update for Windows 7 SP1 and Windows Server 2008 R2 SP1[/b]
[*]Processor: 3GHz Quad-Core
[*]Memory: 8 GB
[*]Hard Drive: [b][i]BioShock[/i] 25GB; [i]BioShock 2[/i] 25GB; [i]BioShock Infinite[/i] 30GB; Total for all three games 80GB[/b]
[*]Video Card: 2GB ATI Radeon HD 7970, 2GB NVIDIA GeForce GTX 770 or better
[*]Sound Card: DirectX Compatible Sound Device[/list]

[b]Some system components such as mobile chipsets, integrated, and AGP graphics cards may be incompatible. Unlisted specifications may not be supported by publisher. [/b]


Relive these award-winning adventures in [b][i]BioShock:  The Collection[/i][/b] on PC September 15, 2016.

notes.title: Remastered BioShock: The Collection Coming to PC on September 15, 2016
notes.content:
[img=https://downloads.2kgames.com/2kblog/bioshock_collection_hero.jpg]

Three [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b] games. All of the single-player DLC. Remastered for modern machines. One value packed bundle. 

It’s been nine years since Irrational Games and 2K took you on a terrifying journey to the depths of the underwater city of Rapture with [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b]. Five years since you returned to Rapture in [b][i]BioShock 2[/i][/b]. Three years since you grabbed a skyhook and sailed across the floating city of Columbia in [b][i]BioShock Infinite[/i][/b]. And on September 15, 2016 (September 15 in Australia and September 16 internationally), you can relive these award-winning adventures or experience them for the very first time remastered for current-gen consoles and digital PC with [b][i]BioShock: The Collection[/i][/b]. 

Working with Blind Squirrel Games, we’ve remastered [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b], [b][i]BioShock 2[/i][/b], and [b][i]BioShock Infinite[/i][/b] making them look better than ever*. [b][i]BioShock: The Collection[/i][/b] brings the three titles together for the first time, complete with all single-player DLC** and a never-before-seen video series, “Director’s Commentary: [i]Imagining BioShock[/i],” which includes insights from Ken Levine – over $100 of content – for only $59.99. It’s a circus of values! And if you already own [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b], [b][i]BioShock 2[/i][/b], and/or [b][i]Minerva’s Den[/i][/b] on Steam, you will be able to upgrade to the remastered version of the respective title(s) for free after release. It’s a circus of values!

If you’ve never experienced the series before, now is the time to play it and see for yourself why the award-winning [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b] franchise has topped countless “Best-Of” lists and garnered more than 125 awards including two BAFTA honors, as well as many Best of E3, Best of Gamescom, and Game of the Year accolades from respected outlets such as [i]IGN, GameSpot, Game Informer,[/i] and many more. The weapons, plasmids, levels, and character models that shocked you years ago have been reskinned and retextured to look better than ever. On top of that, all single-player DLC created for all three games comes loaded in one package. The bundled content for [b][i]BioShock: The Collection[/i][/b] includes:

[img=https://downloads.2kgames.com/2kblog/BioShockTC_Bio1_AndrewRyan_Statue_05.jpg]

[list][*][b][i]BioShock[/i][/b]
[list][*]The video series, “Director’s Commentary: [i]Imagining BioShock[/i],” featuring Ken Levine, creative director on [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b] and [b][i]BioShock Infinite[/i][/b] and Shawn Robertson, animation lead on [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b] and animation director on [b][i]BioShock Infinite[/i][/b].
[*][i]Museum of Orphaned Concepts[/i]: Walk through a Rapture-inspired virtual museum that gives you a behind-the-scenes look at discarded concepts that never made it into the original game.
[*][i]Challenge Rooms[/i]: Outside the story of [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b], tackle puzzles, splicers and Big Daddies. And achievements, of course.[/list][/list]

[img=https://downloads.2kgames.com/2kblog/BioShockTC_Bio2_AdonisLuxuryResort Level.jpg]

[list][*][b][i]BioShock 2[/i][/b] (**Multiplayer will not be included) 
[list][*][i]Minerva’s Den[/i]: A self-contained [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b] story, presenting a side of Rapture you've never seen before. Use expanded combat abilities with the experimental Ion Laser and chaotic Gravity Well Plasmid, unique to Minerva's Den, as you face off against the Lancer Big Daddy. 
[*][i]Protector Trials[/i]: Take control of an Alpha Series Big Daddy woken out of hibernation just before the events of [b][i]BioShock 2[/i][/b].[/list][/list] 

[img=https://downloads.2kgames.com/2kblog/BioShockTC_Bio3_Shot11_Town_Center.jpg]

[list][*][b][i]BioShock Infinite[/i][/b] 
[list][*][i]Burial at Sea - Episode 1 & 2 Add-On Packs[/i]: This major two-part DLC pack completes the [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b] trilogy by taking the series back to where it all began. Return to Rapture just before the events of the original [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b]! 
[*][i]Clash in the Clouds Add-On Pack[/i]: Face 60 waves of challenges across four additional maps for leaderboard glory and unlock areas to explore in The Columbian Archaeological Society hub museum.
[*][i]Columbia's Finest Pack[/i]: Combines the contents of the [i]Industrial Revolution Pack[/i] and the [i]Upgrade Pack[/i] and includes 500 Silver Eagles, five Lock Picks, six unique Gear items, and two weapon upgrades: [i]Comstock’s China Broom Shotgun[/i] and [i]Comstock’s Eagle Eye Sniper Rifle[/i]. [/list][/list]

In short, [b][i]BioShock: The Collection[/i][/b] offers more than $100 of content remastered for PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and digital PC for only $59.99. 

Remember: A man chooses. A slave obeys. So, would you kindly follow the new [url=https://twitter.com/bioshock]@BioShock handle on Twitter[/url], visit us on [url=https://www.facebook.com/bioshock/]Facebook[/url] or go to the [url=https://2k.com/games/bioshock-the-collection]webpage[/url] and prepare for a remastered [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b] experience? 

[b][i]BioShock: The Collection[/i][/b] for Xbox One, PlayStation 4, and PC will be available in North America on September 15, Australia on September 15, and internationally on September 16.

[i]*[b][i]BioShock Infinite[/i][/b] is not being remastered on PC because it already meets current-gen console standards and runs smoothly on high visual settings. 
**[b][i]BioShock: The Collection[/i][/b] will not include [b][i]BioShock 2[/i][/b] multiplayer. [/i]

This post has been updated to reflect the change in the PC launch date.

[i]*[b][i]BioShock Infinite[/i][/b] is not being remastered on PC because it already meets current-gen console standards and runs smoothly on high visual settings. 
**[b][i]BioShock: The Collection[/i][/b] will not include [b][i]BioShock 2[/i][/b] multiplayer. [/i]

This post has been updated to reflect the change in the PC launch date.

tags.feature: Working with Blind Squirrel Games, we’ve remastered [i]BioShock[/i], [i]BioShock 2[/i], and [i]BioShock Infinite[/i] making them look better than ever*. [b][i]BioShock: The Collection[/i][/b] brings the three titles together for the first time, complete with all single-player DLC** and a never-before-seen video series, “Director’s Commentary: [i]Imagining BioShock[/i],” which includes insights from Ken Levine – over $100 of content – for only $59.99.

The video series, “Director’s Commentary: [i]Imagining BioShock[/i],” featuring Ken Levine, creative director on [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b] and [b][i]BioShock Infinite[/i][/b] and Shawn Robertson, animation lead on [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b] and animation director on [b][i]BioShock Infinite[/i][/b].
[i]Museum of Orphaned Concepts[/i]: Walk through a Rapture-inspired virtual museum that gives you a behind-the-scenes look at discarded concepts that never made it into the original game.
[i]Challenge Rooms[/i]: Outside the story of [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b], tackle puzzles, splicers and Big Daddies. And achievements, of course.

[i]Minerva’s Den[/i]: A self-contained [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b] story, presenting a side of Rapture you've never seen before. Use expanded combat abilities with the experimental Ion Laser and chaotic Gravity Well Plasmid, unique to Minerva’s Den, as you face off against the Lancer Big Daddy.
[i]Protector Trials[/i]: Take control of an Alpha Series Big Daddy woken out of hibernation just before the events of [b][i]BioShock 2[/i][/b].

[i]Burial at Sea - Episode 1 & 2 Add-On Packs[/i]: This major two-part DLC pack completes the [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b] trilogy by taking the series back to where it all began. Return to Rapture just before the events of the original [b][i]BioShock[/i][/b]!
[i]Clash in the Clouds Add-On Pack[/i]: Face 60 waves of challenges across four additional maps for leaderboard glory and unlock areas to explore in The Columbian Archaeological Society hub museum.

[i]Columbia's Finest Pack[/i]: Combines the contents of the [i]Industrial Revolution Pack[/i] and the [i]Upgrade Pack[/i] and includes 500 Silver Eagles, five Lock Picks, six unique Gear items, and two weapon upgrades: [i]Comstock’s China Broom Shotgun[/i] and [i]Comstock’s Eagle Eye Sniper Rifle[/i].

notes.title: For $30, BioShock Ultimate Rapture Edition Includes Two Full Games, All the DLC and New Unseen Artwork
notes.content:
Sad that this March's BioShock Infinite won't be set in Rapture? You'll get a chance to re-visit the beautiful underwater city of the first two BioShock games with the newly announced Ultimate Rapture edition, which will boast an all-new Museum of Orphaned Concepts filled with concept art and character designs that weren't used for Irrational's hit franchise. The new bundle comes out on Jan. 14 for the PS3 and Xbox 360, at a cost of $30. Here's a full rundown of what's inside:

• Museum of Orphaned Concepts: Take a tour of a never-before-seen BioShock museum and view early concept art, character models and more set within the halls of Rapture.
• Plasmids Pack: Includes four additional Plasmids and Gene Tonics—Sonic Boom, EVE Saver, Vending Expert and Machine Buster—for use in BioShock.
• Challenge Rooms Pack: Previously exclusive to PS3™ and now available for Xbox 360 for the first time, the pack tests the player's mettle by requiring them to utilize the skills learned while traversing the halls of Rapture to survive three separate puzzle rooms in BioShock.
• Sinclair Solutions Tester: Contains a number of customization features that allow players to further their character's development in BioShock 2 multiplayer modes and provides a deeper multiplayer experience.
• Rapture Metro: Includes six additional multiplayer maps, an additional multiplayer gameplay mode and a rank increase to level 50 for BioShock 2 multiplayer.
• The Protector Trials: Features frantic combat and fast-paced action designed to push players' mastery of weapons and Plasmids in a BioShock 2 single-player experience spread across six maps.
• Minerva's Den: A substantial narrative experience that puts players in the role Subject Sigma and introduces new characters, locations and mystery to the world of Rapture in BioShock 2. Set in a new environment, Rapture Central Computing, Minerva's Den adds a gripping new storyline to extend the BioShock 2 experience.
• Also included, is an exclusive collectable sticker pack from BioShock Infinite's world of Columbia to get gamers ready for the next chapter in the BioShock universe.
